title: Gray Zone Warfare's player count jumps by over 1000% following its most recent update: 'Players are coming back'
partialText: The extraction shooter had over 126,000 daily active players after its Spearhead patch.

title: Your joys will always be someone else's junk
partialText: People don't like a game I've been playing, and that's okay.

title: A Japanese indie developer is seeking legal action over alleged missing funds from a crowdfunding campaign, says the funding platform claims the money was 'mistakenly wired to a different client'
partialText: The successor to 428: Shibuya Scramble suffers a bizarre financial setback.

title: Marathon's most powerful gun gets a major nerf, as Bungie seeks to 'curb a little bit of its dominion in the game'
partialText: Biotoxic Disinjector gets a big damage reduction.

title: Star Wars Zero Company studio founder praises Lucasfilm and Respawn for taking a chance on a tactics game
partialText: "Looking at some of the things going on in the industry, it's very derivative. Art is always that way."

title: Star Wars Zero Company writer wants its cast to have real friction: 'It's not a personal fantasy game'
partialText: "Player-centric romance" and chosen ones have been cast aside for more tenuous team dynamics.

title: 'Blockchain-powered' game storefront reportedly shutting down and taking customers' games with it
partialText: The storefront, founded by Brian Fargo, appears to be a wilting leftover from the crypto craze.

title: In 2007, two game music GOATs collaborated on the criminally underrated soundtrack to a similarly underrated D&D RPG
partialText: The realheads know a Brandon-Schaffer collab is where it's at.

title: Never doubt the commitment of horse-girl fans: Umamusume cosplayers are having actual races at tracks around the world
partialText: Real-life races have taken place in Malaysia, Thailand, Peru, and the US.

title: I tried to become a pro bowler but I skipped one important step: learning how to bowl
partialText: My attempt to rise through the ranks of PBA Pro Bowling 2026 hit a small and completely unexpected snag.

title: After over 150 hours with Crimson Desert, it still makes no damn sense—compels me though
partialText: It's a hard game to pin down.

title: Tarn Adams, co-creator of Dwarf Fortress, has over 1,400 hours in Factorio and is currently obsessed with terraforming games: 'Dwarf Fortress just doesn't accommodate a full-on sci-fi thing'
partialText: Bay 12 Games' co-founder talks playing The Planet Crafter, Beast, and more than 40 years of saved desktops.

title: It's not just Arrow Lake that's been refreshed: Intel's whole approach to the consumer market seems like a new direction
partialText: Talk is cheap, listening is priceless.

title: Thank goodness Magic: The Gathering isn't doing a Harry Potter crossover set
partialText: Instead it's returning to Strixhaven, a less problematic wizard school and part of Magic's existing multiverse.

title: A new Crimson Desert patch adds the only RPG feature that matters: A hide helmet button
partialText: Show us that jawline, Kliff.

title: Our first look at Alex Garland's Elden Ring movie might be in this leaked set footage from a lucky fan in the UK
partialText: Hey, I know that church.

title: Datamined Elden Ring cutscene gives more clues about DLC villain Miquella's original story
partialText: Cryptic as always.

title: Warframe community director says 'nothing in our games will be AI-generated, ever'
partialText: Cephalons aside, Warframe will remain AI-free.

title: Amazon TV head allegedly orders Mass Effect show rewrite to make it 'more appealing to non-gamers'
partialText: I should go.

title: Fallout: New Vegas for the PS3 mod adds Fallout: New Vegas for the PS3 to Fallout: New Vegas for the PC
partialText: Also Fallout 3.

title: I bought a PS5 on launch day but I won't be buying a PS6, even though its exclusives aren't coming to PC anymore
partialText: How much for the funky white box!?

title: Final Fantasy 14's latest variant dungeon is so good, it deserves better—the MMO needs to figure out its rewards so all this great work isn't wasted
partialText: Just let me get gear, please.

title: MindsEye is a glitchy, incoherent mess I wouldn't recommend to anyone—and it might also be my favorite game of 2026
partialText: Look, it's complicated.

title: This Nightdive-remastered 3DO shooter shows why it took Halo to break PC gaming's FPS hegemony
partialText: Playing PO'ed will make you feel exactly like that.

title: Subscription service for indie games gets a rough reception
partialText: Indie Pass was announced this week, and a lot of people are saying 'no thanks.'

title: The best tool for playing obscure old PC games now supports the sublime FMV cheese of Crime Patrol 2: Drug Wars and a Lovecraftian adventure one YouTuber scored a 'terribly low 2/10'
partialText: You've got to be morbidly curious now, right?

title: This AI startup envisions '100 million new people' making videogames
partialText: Tesana says we can create our "dream game" with prompts, but would 100 million people doing that actually be "exciting"?

title: Slay the Spire 2 adds end-of-run badges 'to let you know what was unique about each adventure' in latest beta patch
partialText: The update, available in the public beta branch, makes numerous reworks, tweaks, and fixes, and so far hasn't sparked nearly the level of backlash the last one got.

title: Magazine generates fake AI interview with One Piece actor Mackenyu
partialText: The faux interview "was produced with Claude, Copilot, and edited by humans."

title: Get the Homeworld Remastered Collection, Deserts of Kharak, and 8 more RTS games for just $8
partialText: Homeworld and Deserts of Kharak are worth the price of admission on their own.

title: 'There's always the chance s**t hits the fan and we suffer another major setback,' Skyblivion lead says about the possibility of another delay, but 'from what I see internally I am pretty optimistic'
partialText: The Skyblivion development team put out a new call for help earlier this week, and it led some (including me) to wonder if another delay is coming.

title: Google AI embarrasses itself when asked to perform the one simple task computers have always been good at
partialText: If you're going to force me to talk to the computer, it better be smarter than this.

title: Beloved YouTuber The Gaming Historian moves on from making videos with a 'parting gift': A ton of ancient Nintendo court docs you can browse on the Internet Archive
partialText: The docs are from what may be the company's most famous lawsuit.

title: 'There are times when you want to put GTA down and pick up something else,' Samson studio founder says: 'I think there's a space for us there'
partialText: Comparisons are inevitable, but Liquid Swords founder Christofer Sundberg sees his rough-and-tumble crime sim as a more of a side game than a GTA competitor.

title: House Flipper is free to keep on Steam for the next few days
partialText: Try out the renovate-'em-up's original incarnation before the remaster comes out.

title: Our favorite open world FPS indie gem is getting New Game+, Spider-Man swinging, and wallrunning later this month
partialText: Another excuse to play more Echo Point Nova? How could I refuse?

title: State of Decay 3 springs back to life to announce alpha tests in May
partialText: You can sign up now for a shot at access.

title: Rust is getting hydro power through water wheels that can also be powered by humans: 'Before you ask, yes, you can force handcuffed players into them'
partialText: Facepunch's latest update also adds armoured ladder hatches, coloured buttons, and Easter-themed bunny costumes

title: Petit Planet, the upcoming 'cozy galactic life sim' from HoYoVerse, is taking signups for a new beta test happening later this month
partialText: There's still no release date, but it's getting closer.

title: After 36 years at the legendary FPS studio, Raven Software co-founder Brian Raffel is retiring
partialText: Raffel has led the Heretic and Call of Duty developer since its foundation.

title: Bungie provides details on Marathon's imminent Recon buff 'by popular demand', revealing an improved Echo Pulse and a 'more aggressive' tracker drone
partialText: Recon's area scanning ability will soon distinguish between AI and human enemies.

title: Take-Two has seemingly laid off an unspecified portion of its AI team, including its head of AI
partialText: Luke Dicken, who previously spent a decade with Zynga, says his time with the company "has come to an end".

title: A former GameStop exec thought building its Steam competitor would be his 'forever job,' but the retailer bet the house on digital distribution being 'a passing phase'
partialText: This Picasso hack will never make it as a painter!

title: Mega Crit co-founder says he wasn't bothered by the Steam backlash to Slay the Spire 2's beta balance patch: 'It's difficult for players to feel like they're heard'
partialText: Casey Yano says that, ultimately, reviewers are just using the tools they're given.

title: The Emperor Protects: A Warhammer 40,000 Musical is a deeply committed April Fool's joke from Games Workshop, and I don't care if it's a day late because it's just that good
partialText: "Just because there is only war, doesn't mean there can't also be music."

title: Revisiting the last truly great Call of Duty
partialText: Why a lot of people are playing a seven-year-old CoD again.

title: 43% of you have, or will be switching to gaming on Linux this year, but more surprising than that over a quarter of you actually don't mind Windows
partialText: Aww bless, Windows is really not that bad after all is it? But Linux is fun.

title: A contributor to GameStop's long-forgotten Steam competitor explains why he thinks Valve came out on top: 'What Steam did better than anybody else was to create a community'
partialText: In hindsight, who would have guessed that Valve would win against the likes of Microsoft, EA, or Ubisoft?

title: Warren Spector's multiplayer Thief successor changes direction: Instead of PvPvE, it's now focusing on 2-player co-op and singleplayer
partialText: Otherside says that as development has progressed, it's become clear that singleplayer and co-op is just more fun.

title: Slay the Spire 2's team is already cooking on 3 ideas for new game modes, each offering 'ways to interact with Slay the Spire that don't exist right now'
partialText: Can you deduce precisely what Mega Crit is working on?
